title: 12 Things a Virtual Assistant Can Take Off Your Plate
description: Not sure what to hand off to a virtual assistant? Here are 12 everyday tasks a VA can handle for your small business or creator brand, so you can get back to the work only you can do.
intro: Most small business owners wait way too long to get help. Not because they can't use it, but because they're not sure what they'd even hand off. If you've ever said "it's faster if I just do it myself," this list is for you.

p: 1. Sorting your email so only what needs you reaches you.
2. Answering common questions in your DMs and comments, in your voice.
3. Following up with people who reached out and never heard back.
4. Scheduling your posts a week or a month ahead.
5. Making simple Canva graphics, quote posts, and story templates.
6. Turning one podcast episode or blog post into several smaller posts.
7. Writing and updating Etsy or shop listings, titles, and tags.
8. Keeping an eye on orders, messages, and reviews.
9. Updating prices, photos, and seasonal listings so your shop never looks stale.
10. Writing and sending your monthly newsletter.
11. Making small website updates: new pages, links, and fixes.
12. Building a freebie or quiz that grows your email list while you sleep.
For one week, write down every task that made you sigh. Circle the ones that don't need your brain, just your time. That's your first hand-off list.
You don't need 40 hours of help. Most small businesses start with five or ten hours a month, and that alone can feel like breathing room.

title: How to Grow Your Email List with a Quiz (Even If You're Not Techy)
description: A simple, step-by-step way to use a personality-style quiz to grow your email list, from picking a topic to writing results people actually want to share.
intro: People love learning something about themselves. That's why a good quiz is one of the easiest ways to turn a casual follower into someone on your email list. Here's how it works, start to finish.

sections.h: 1. Pick a question your audience already asks
p: The best quizzes answer something people wonder about anyway. What's my style? What's holding me back? Which product is right for me?
If you sell candles, it might be "What's your cozy season scent?" If you're a coach, it might be "What's your burnout pattern?"
Eight to ten questions is the sweet spot. Long enough to feel real, short enough that people finish. Four result types is plenty.
Write each result like a small mirror: what this pattern looks like, why it makes sense, and one gentle next step. If it feels true, people screenshot it and send it to friends.

sections.h: 4. Ask for the email right before the result
p: After the last question, ask for an email to see the result. Since they're already invested, most people say yes. Be honest about what they'll get from you after.

sections.h: 5. Connect it to your next step
p: Every result should point somewhere: a product, a freebie, a booking link. That's how a fun quiz quietly becomes your best salesperson.
Every quiz on this site was built this way. Take one to see how it feels from the other side, and if you'd like one for your business, I can build it for you.

title: The Weekly Etsy Tasks You Can Hand Off (and the Ones You Shouldn't)
description: Running an Etsy shop takes more than making things. Here are the weekly Etsy tasks you can hand to a virtual assistant, and the few that should stay with you.
intro: I run my own Etsy shop, so I know the truth: making the product is the fun part. Everything around it is what wears you out. Here's how to split it up.

p: Writing listing titles, descriptions, and all 13 tags.
Refreshing older listings so they show up in search again.
Making listing images and mockups in Canva.
Answering common buyer questions with saved replies.
Keeping track of sales, reviews, and what's selling best.
Sharing new listings to Pinterest and Instagram.
Creating the actual products. That's your magic.
Deciding your prices and what you make next.
Personal replies to buyers who had a problem. A real note from the owner goes a long way.
Monday: check messages and orders. Wednesday: add or refresh two listings. Friday: share your best sellers on social.
That's it. Small, steady updates beat a big overhaul every few months.
I can take the listing work, the graphics, and the posting off your hands, so your shop keeps moving while you make things.
